arms.diagnostic_note: The k=5 endgame optimization works exactly as predicted. Score remains at the ceiling of 100. The BFS at n=11 with cross-n verification (n=20,50,100,500,1000) produced generalizable endgame sequences. Average ops (1986.0) matches the prediction precisely. The 119-case dispatch handles all non-identity permutations of the last 5 elements in 2-5 operations, with the 4 hardest cases (needing 5 ops) being: [n-3,n-4,n-2,n,n-1], [n-3,n-4,n,n-1,n-2], [n-2,n-3,n-4,n,n-1], [n-1,n-2,n-3,n-4,n]. The improvement over k=4 is marginal but confirms the optimization pattern: each step up in endgame size k saves 2 main-loop ops at the cost of at most 1 endgame op.
